Subject: Pricing exhibit v3 — caps/floors (order schedule)

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the call yesterday — attaching the latest order form with our in-line pricing exhibit edits. A few points we want to make explicit so legal can move quickly: 

- Minimum monthly commitment (Section 2.1): we can accept a rolling minimum, but it needs to be capped to avoid a sudden step-up at peak months.
- Floor true-up timing (Section 4): we prefer quarterly true-ups to align with our billing cycle.
- Cap on unit price increases (Section 6): any upward reprice should be capped to the CPI + 2% and only once per 12 months.
- Escrow/credit mechanics: if you require credit-hold protection for burst capacity, we need a clear earnback path.

Attached: datapulse_orderform_pricingexhibit_v3.pdf — redline from my side. Can you provide a redwood-preferred markup and a short playbook on how you'd operationalize the floor/cap language (what triggers true-ups, how credits reconcile)?

We'd like to get to agreement this month. Mason (cc) is helping with legal; he may suggest alternate wording.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Procurement, DataPulse
ProcureOps | datapulse.io

Elena — thanks for the redline and clear bullets. Quick response while I sync with Ops and Legal: 

High-level proposal (we'll send a marked-up):
1) Minimum smoothing: agree to a rolling monthly minimum with a 3-month lookback average to avoid sudden step-ups. This means only if trailing 3-month average usage exceeds the stated band will the next billing month reflect an upgraded minimum.
2) Quarterly true-ups: we can do quarterly true-ups aligned to your billing quarter. True-ups reconcile usage vs. minimums and produce either an invoice for underage or a credit for overage.
3) Cap on increases: acceptable to Redwood to bound price increases to CPI + 2% measured annually, but need to limit reprice to specific contract events (e.g., new major feature tiers or infrastructure-cost pass-throughs). We'll propose precise trigger language.
4) Escrow / earnback: propose an operational earnback where 50% of any stabilization credit is earned back if usage grows 20%+ over a 6-month moving window; otherwise credit offsets fees over next two quarters.

Action items: I will circulate a concise redline (two-page excerpt) that implements the above and includes a short operational playbook for finance and Customer Ops (who handles true-up notices, timing, ledger treatment). Laura will take point on the legal text; Stephanie will include the ops runbook and example reconciliation table.

Expect a marked-up by EOD tomorrow. If you have must-not-change items call them out now.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Markus / Elena — quick note from legal: a couple of drafting items we'll flag in markup: 

- "Trailing 3-month average" is workable, but prefer to define exactly which usage metrics feed the average (e.g., billable tokens vs. total tokens).
- For CPI link: define CPI series (US All Urban Consumers) and a floor of 0% (no deflation credits). Also add an upper annual notification window (60 days prior).
- Escrow / earnback: need a cap on aggregate earnback to avoid open-ended liability for Redwood (suggest 75% of stabilization credit).

I can take Laura's draft and apply these guardrails; happy to talk through the earnback calculation off-thread.

Cheers,

Elena, Mason — attached is Redwood's proposed excerpt and an operational playbook (two pages) that maps the contract language to Finance / CS steps. Highlights: 

- Defined metrics: billable_tokens (generation + context) will be the usage metric for smoothing and true-up.
- Trailing average: trailing 3-month arithmetic mean of billable_tokens triggers change in minimum for the next billing period; explicit examples included.
- True-up timing: invoices generated within 30 days of quarter close, credits applied to next invoice.
- Reprice cap: CPI-U + 2% annual cap; Redwood to provide 60 days' notice; no retroactive increases.
- Stabilization credit earnback: capped at 75% of originally granted amount; earned back pro rata over six months if usage increases per threshold.

Please review the attached markup and playbook. If this aligns we can move to a short signatures-only addendum and a DocuSign envelope for the order schedule.

Next steps: Elena — can you confirm by Monday whether the earnback cap and CPI spec are acceptable? If yes, we'll route to Mason for a 1-hour markup call on Tuesday.

Thanks,
